name: @slyte/mcp

tools.name: search_slyte_docs
tools.description: Semantic search across the Slyte framework documentation. Start here for any new topic. Returns the best-matching pages (miniContent) plus related pages and detailed refPages via 2-level expansion. Accumulate the returned `servedKeys` and pass them back to skip pages the client already has.

query.description: ONE narrow 3-7 word query combining a canonical term + intent, e.g. "router transition hooks". Issue separate calls per concept.

maxResults.description: Max top-level results. Use 2-3 for focused lookups, up to 10 for broad exploration.

domain.description: HARD filter — restrict results to URLs under this path (e.g., "/doc", "/uiComponents", "/dom"). Use ONLY when you are CERTAIN; it EXCLUDES everything else. Prefer `scope` for a softer hint.

scope.description: SOFT hint (recommended) — a URL path fragment matching the intent, e.g. "/doc" for a framework concept (router, data, service, route, lifecycle), "/uiComponents" for a UI widget/plugin, "/dom" for a DOM utility. Boosts matching pages WITHOUT excluding others, so a wrong guess still returns the right page. Set it whenever the query names a framework concept that could collide with a similarly-named UI component (e.g. "lazy route" vs the lazyload plugin).

servedKeys.description: Content keys the client already has — pass back the `servedKeys` array most recently returned (if you made calls in parallel, union their `servedKeys` arrays first).

tools.name: search_slyte_sections
tools.description: Section/heading-based search over the docs (NOT meaning-based). Matches your query against each page's section HEADINGS (case/space/underscore-insensitive — e.g. "form events" finds the "Form events" section), then returns the matching section's PARENT PAGE content plus which section matched, with a heading-match `score` per result. Best when you know the section name, an exact heading, or an API/method name. It does NOT silently fall back to semantic: when no heading matches strongly it returns a ⚠️ low-confidence note — for fuzzy/conceptual intent use search_slyte_hybrid (best) or search_slyte_docs. Accumulate the returned `servedKeys` and pass them back to skip pages the client already has.

query.description: Words from the section HEADING you want, e.g. "form events", "lifecycle hooks", "$L.ajax". Matched against section headings first, body text as a weak fallback.

maxResults.description: How many top pages get their FULL content included (default 5). The grouped match list shows more matches than this; open any of them with get_slyte_page.

scope.description: OPTIONAL area filter — a URL fragment like "/dom", "/doc", "/uiComponents". OMIT it (default) to search ALL modules: results are spread across every area that matched (the single best match still leads). Set it only to restrict matches to one area.

servedKeys.description: Content keys the client already has — pass back the `servedKeys` array most recently returned.

tools.name: search_slyte_hybrid
tools.description: HYBRID search — the best default for most queries. Fuses MEANING (semantic embeddings) with exact HEADING matches (the section index): it finds the right pages by intent AND boosts exact heading/API-name matches, attaching the matched section's #anchor so the result points to the exact spot. Use this when you're not sure whether the query is conceptual or an exact term. Accumulate the returned `servedKeys` and pass them back to skip pages the client already has.

query.description: Your query — conceptual ("how do I validate a form") or an exact term/heading/API name ("form events", "$L.ajax"). Hybrid handles both.

maxResults.description: Max pages to return with full content.

scope.description: Optional area filter — a URL fragment like "/dom", "/doc", "/uiComponents".

servedKeys.description: Content keys the client already has — pass back the `servedKeys` array most recently returned.

tools.name: get_slyte_topic
tools.description: Get documentation for a specific Slyte framework topic. By default returns the topic's overview (miniContent), related documentation (miniContent), and detailed refPages (markdownContent) via 2-level expansion. Use includeRelated=false when you only need the main topic page. Accumulate the returned `servedKeys` and pass them back to skip pages the client already has.

includeRelated.description: Whether to expand and include related URLs content. Set to false for a focused single-page lookup. Defaults to true.

servedKeys.description: Content keys the client already has — pass back EXACTLY the `servedKeys` array most recently returned by any tool on this server.

tools.name: get_slyte_page
tools.description:
Fetch the content of a single documentation page deterministically. Surgical precision tool — zero search, zero expansion, zero recursion.

PREREQUISITE — You MUST already have Slyte framework context before calling this tool (from a prior get_slyte_topic or search_slyte_docs call). Do NOT call this as your first documentation retrieval step.

Content selection (first available wins): 1. miniContent  2. content.
If the client already has :mini for this page, the response upgrades to full markdownContent.

page.description: Full URL or exact topic path. Examples: "components/templates", "uiComponents/button/overview"

servedKeys.description: Content keys the client already has — pass back EXACTLY the `servedKeys` array most recently returned. If this page is already known at :full, the server returns a pointer via `skippedKeys`. If only :mini is known, it upgrades to full markdownContent.

tools.name: get_slyte_ui_component_css
tools.description: Get the ACTUAL CSS or LESS for a UI component or plugin (e.g. `button`, `dropdown`, `draggable`, `lazyload`), read live from the developer's own installed @slyte/lyte-ui-component package — not a static snapshot. Returns both the component's style rules and its CSS custom-property (theming) declarations in the requested format. Call this whenever a component or plugin is looked up and its styling is needed — do not invent CSS variable names.

component.description: Component or plugin slug (e.g. "button", "dropdown", "draggable"), or a topic path like "uiComponents/button/overview" — the slug is extracted automatically.

format.description: 'css' = compiled, theme-variable-linked CSS (default). 'less' = the raw LESS source.

theme.description: Which theme's CSS-variable values to read (default: 'default' / light theme).

tools.name: get_slyte_instructions
tools.description: Get the Slyte framework core coding rules, CLI command reference, and documentation domains. Returns essential rules for generating correct Slyte code. For coding guardrails (action vs method, this context, data mutation, template syntax), call `get_slyte_guardrails` with the relevant topic instead. Accepts `servedKeys` — if `__instructions__` is already known, returns a pointer via `skippedKeys`.

servedKeys.description: Content keys the client already has — pass back EXACTLY the `servedKeys` array most recently returned. If it includes `__instructions__`, the server returns a pointer only.

tools.name: guide_new_slyte_app
tools.description: Get step-by-step instructions for creating a new Slyte application. Returns CLI commands, folder structure, key files, npm packages, ES module imports, and script include order for scaffolding a Slyte app from scratch.

tools.name: get_slyte_guardrails
tools.description: Get the pre-flight checklist for a specific coding area — MUST be called before creating or editing files. Also call with topic 'data' when any module (component, route, service, etc.) uses data store operations (getAll, getEntity, newEntity, $db, store.findAll, etc.). Returns decision trees, correct syntax patterns, and common anti-patterns. Accepts `servedKeys` — if the topic sentinel is already known, returns a pointer via `skippedKeys`.

topic.description: The coding area: 'component' (authoring a component's JS structure: data()/actions/methods/lookups — start here), 'uicomponent' (USING Slyte's <lyte-*> UI-component library: prefer/compose, markup pattern, overlays/modal, $L wiring, lyte-table, prohibited APIs), 'component-js', 'component-template', 'route', 'data' (also for ANY module using data store ops), 'service', 'ux' (DESIGNING/BUILDING a whole screen or app UI — the build-order shell→archetype→states→components-by-intent→polish→verify + the intent→component map; call BEFORE laying out a screen's markup), 'review' (REVIEWING/critiquing existing Slyte code: severity levels + review workflow + a Slyte anti-pattern checklist)

servedKeys.description: Content keys the client already has — pass back EXACTLY the `servedKeys` array most recently returned. Guardrail responses use the sentinel `__guardrails:<topic>__`.

tools.name: list_slyte_topics
tools.description: List all available Slyte documentation topics, grouped by area.

tools.name: clear_slyte_session
tools.description: Clear the session dedup cache so subsequent get_slyte_topic/search_slyte_docs return full content instead of treating URLs as already served. Use when you need a fresh documentation context in the same session.

tools.name: get_slyte_ui_component
tools.description: Focused context for ONE Slyte UI component or plugin — its overview, description, and primary usage — in a single lean, token-light response. Use this when the model needs the context of a specific component (e.g. "button", "modal", "dropdown", "draggable") without the broader related-page expansion of get_slyte_topic. For that component's exact API (props/events/methods) call get_slyte_component_api; for its styles call get_slyte_ui_component_css.

tools.name: get_slyte_component_api
tools.description: Lean API lookup for ONE Slyte UI component/plugin — returns just its properties, events, methods and utilities (the API surface), WITHOUT the full page or related-page expansion. Use this instead of search_slyte_docs / get_slyte_topic when you only need a component's API to wire it up: the response is small and stays well under the token limit.

tools.name: verify_slyte_setup
tools.description: Doctor / pre-flight + code-review check for a Slyte app. Auto-discovers the app in the working directory (or a subfolder) and verifies: (1) @slyte/lyte-dom + @slyte/lyte-ui-component declared as dependencies, (2) `$L` wired in app.js (`import $L from "@slyte/lyte-dom"; window.$L = $L;`), (3) the UI-component CSS <link> uses the inner /dist/ path, (4) **UI-COMPONENT USAGE — scans templates/JS for raw `<button>`/`<table>`/`<select>`/`<dialog>`/`alert()`/hand-built modals and FAILS the check when a Slyte UI component should have been used instead** (a hand-rolled equivalent is a defect, not a style choice), (5) @slyte/core + @slyte/cli match the pinned build. Returns a ✓/✗ report with fixes. Run it after writing code / before declaring the app done to catch a generic-HTML build that ignored the UI library.

instructions:
Authoritative documentation server for the Slyte framework. Always query these tools for syntax, conventions, and APIs rather than relying on pre-trained knowledge.

### ⛔ MANDATORY TRIGGER — read first

This workspace is a **Slyte framework** project. Treat ANY request to create, scaffold, build, or add a feature to an app / game / page / component / route / UI here as a **Slyte** task — **even if the user never says "Slyte."** BEFORE writing or editing ANY file:
1. **New app** → call `guide_new_slyte_app`, then scaffold with the `slyte` CLI (`slyte new` / `slyte generate`) — NOT hand-written files.
2. **Component / route / data / service code** → call `get_slyte_guardrails` for that topic.
3. **Reviewing code** → `get_slyte_guardrails({ topic: "review" })`.

**NEVER emit application code from pre-trained knowledge** — no generic `<!DOCTYPE html>`, vanilla-JS, or React app. If you are about to write a non-Slyte file, STOP: that is the wrong approach here. If the framework is unstated, assume Slyte. If you cannot load/use these tools, say so before writing any code — do not silently fall back to a generic build.

### ⛔ UI COMPONENTS ARE MANDATORY — not optional

For EVERY visual element, use the Slyte UI component if one exists — do NOT hand-roll raw HTML for something the library already provides. The following in a template are **DEFECTS**, not style choices:
- a raw `<button>` → use `<lyte-button>`
- a raw `<table>` → use `<lyte-table>`
- `alert()` or a hand-built modal / dialog / popup → use `<lyte-modal>`
- a hand-built dropdown / select / checkbox / input / tabs / accordion / tooltip → use the matching `<lyte-*>`

BEFORE writing ANY template markup you MUST:
1. List each visual element the UI needs.
2. For each, call `search_slyte_hybrid` / `get_slyte_ui_component` to find its `<lyte-*>` component, and OUTPUT an **element → chosen `lyte-*` component (or a justified raw-HTML exception)** table.
3. Raw HTML is allowed ONLY for genuinely bespoke visuals with no library equivalent (e.g. a custom game board) — and only after you confirmed no `<lyte-*>` fits.

**If you are about to skip a UI component / go "dependency-free", you MUST ASK the user first** ("this would use raw `<button>`/`<table>` instead of `lyte-button`/`lyte-table` — confirm?"). Deciding unilaterally to avoid the UI library is a defect. Call `get_slyte_guardrails({ topic: "uicomponent" })` for discovery + composition, run `verify_slyte_setup` (it flags raw buttons/tables/modals it finds), and run `get_slyte_guardrails({ topic: "review" })` BEFORE declaring the app done.

### Tool Selection

| Intent | Tool | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Search docs — DEFAULT (unsure / conceptual / mixed) | `search_slyte_hybrid` | **Best default.** Fuses meaning + exact-heading: exact terms lead, concepts find the right page with its `#anchor`. |
| Search docs by MEANING / concept | `search_slyte_docs` | Pure semantic search — fuzzy/conceptual questions. Use `maxResults: 2-3` for focused queries. |
| Search docs by an exact HEADING / API name | `search_slyte_sections` | Heading/section match (case/space-insensitive) — best when you know a heading or API/method (e.g. `"form events"`, `"$L.ajax"`). It does NOT auto-fall-back: when no heading matches strongly it returns a ⚠️ low-confidence note — then switch to `search_slyte_hybrid` or `search_slyte_docs`. |
| Deep-dive on a topic | `get_slyte_topic` | Set `includeRelated: false` when context is already established. |
| Fetch a specific page | `get_slyte_page` | Surgical lookup; use only after identifying the path. |
| Style a component / plugin | `get_slyte_ui_component_css` | Inspects live package CSS/LESS variables. Run before authoring styles. |
| Design / lay out a screen or app UI | `get_slyte_guardrails({ topic: "ux" })` | Build-order (shell → archetype → the 4 states → components-by-intent → polish → verify) + the intent→component map. Call BEFORE writing a screen's markup, so the right `lyte-*` is a lookup, not a guess. |
| Write / edit application code | `get_slyte_guardrails` | Mandatory before writing **or editing** (incl. adding an action/method to an existing component). Topics: `component`, `component-js`, `component-template`, `uicomponent`, `route`, `data`, `service`, `ux`. |
| Review / critique existing Slyte code | `get_slyte_guardrails({ topic: "review" })` | Severity levels + review workflow + a Slyte anti-pattern checklist. |
| Browse all topics | `list_slyte_topics` | Lists available topics across all domains. |
| Scaffold a new application | `guide_new_slyte_app` | Step-by-step setup guide. |
| CLI rules & full reference | `get_slyte_instructions` | Session-level reference. |
| Reset cache | `clear_slyte_session` | Clears session state if responses become stale. |

### Core Rules
- **CLI Scaffolding:** Always generate boilerplate via CLI (`slyte new`, `slyte generate ... --defaults`). Do not hand-author boilerplate files. **If the CLI errors or hangs, STOP and tell the user it is a CLI problem — do NOT silently hand-author** (hand-authoring is a last resort, only with the user's explicit approval).
- **Session Deduplication:** Always pass the accumulated `servedKeys` array back in subsequent tool calls to prevent duplicated payloads.
- **Component scope:** everything the component owns lives INSIDE the component class — `data()`, `static actions()`, `static methods()`, `static observers()`, `lookups()`, AND the data it renders. Put render/seed data DIRECTLY in `data()` as `prop(type, { default: <value> })` — **never** a module-level `const`/`let` or `static` data field. **Component logic and helpers are INSTANCE METHODS** (`someHelper(){…}` on the class, called `this.someHelper()`) — never module-level functions, even to "share" a helper between `data()` and an action. **Computed data** (built by a function) uses an empty `default` and is built in `init()` via `this.setData(...)` calling those instance methods. After imports, **module scope stays empty** — no data, no functions, no logic outside the class. **The same scope rule applies to every Slyte module — routes, services, and schemas: all data, hooks, and logic live inside the class.** When ADDING an action/method to an EXISTING component, put it in that component's EXISTING `static actions()`/`static methods()` return object — **one block per class**; never a second block, a module-level function, or code outside the class body. (Editing a component is still "coding" — read `get_slyte_guardrails({ topic: "component" })` first.)
- **Authoritative Docs:** Never invent undocumented syntax. If an API is missing from documentation, state the gap clearly.
